title: [rereview] project-LICHEN-y0vp: Rust DAO-ACK flags byte has K=1,D=0 but DODAGID present (RFC 6550 violation)
description:
In commit fdaffad86, rust/lichen-node/src/rpl_stack.rs line 1350: ack_body[1] = 0x80. Per RFC 6550 §6.5, the DAO-ACK base object byte 1 has:
- Bit 7 = K (1 = this ACK acknowledges an ACK-requested DAO) ✓
- Bit 6 = D (1 = DODAGID field present)

Setting byte[1] = 0x80 sets K=1, D=0. But bytes 4-19 contain the DODAGID (line 1353). Any RFC-compliant receiver seeing D=0 will expect a 4-byte DAO-ACK base and interpret bytes 4-19 as trailing options, not as DODAGID, leading to parser confusion.

Additionally, the C-side function lichen_rpl_dao_ack_write in messages.c:235 has the same class of bug: it writes d_byte = 0x80 | (ack->flags & 0x7F) when d_flag is true, but D is bit 6 (0x40), not bit 7 (0x80). The C code should be writing d_byte = 0x40 | (ack->flags & 0x3F). This DAO-ACK write bug was NOT introduced by this commit but is nevertheless a prerequisite bug for the DAO-ACK feature to work.

Fix (Rust): ack_body[1] = 0xC0 (K=1, D=1).
Fix (C messages.c:235): d_byte = (d_flag ? 0x40 : 0) | (ack->flags & 0x3F).
